text: Mainly because they fit into busy lives. You can listen while you drive, exercise or do housework, so they don't compete with other activities the way videos do. They're also very personal — you choose exactly what interests you, from history to cooking, instead of waiting for a radio programme. And because anyone can start one cheaply, there's an enormous variety of voices and topics.

tips.en: Don't compete the way videos do explains the convenience precisely.
tips.kk: Don't compete … the way videos do — ыңғайлылықты дәл түсіндіру.
tips.ru: Don't compete … the way videos do — точное объяснение удобства.
tips.example: they don't compete with other activities the way videos do

tips.en: Convenience, personal choice and variety make a full answer.
tips.kk: Ыңғайлылық, жеке таңдау, алуан түрлілік — жауап толық.
tips.ru: Удобство, личный выбор, разнообразие — ответ полный.
tips.example: there's an enormous variety of voices and topics

questions.question: Why have podcasts become so popular?

text: I think it depends on what you're learning. Listening is great for getting the big picture and staying motivated, because a good speaker can make almost any topic come alive. But for detailed or technical information, reading is usually more effective — you can go back, underline things and move at your own pace. Ideally, I'd combine them: listen first for interest, then read to go deeper.

tips.en: Listening for the big picture, reading for details — a clear division.
tips.kk: Listening жалпы көрініс үшін, reading нақты мәлімет үшін — анық бөлу.
tips.ru: Listening для общей картины, reading для деталей — чёткое разделение.
tips.example: Listening is great for getting the big picture

tips.en: Listen first, then read gives a practical conclusion.
tips.kk: Listen first …, then read — практикалық қорытынды.
tips.ru: Listen first …, then read — практичный итог.
tips.example: listen first for interest, then read to go deeper

note.en: “As fast or slow as you like”.

questions.question: Is it better to learn from listening or from reading?

text: Yes, I think trust has fallen quite a lot, especially among younger people. Part of the reason is that anyone can now point out a newspaper's mistakes online within minutes, so errors are much more visible. Another factor is that many people feel traditional media represent official views rather than ordinary people's concerns. Ironically, though, some of them then trust random bloggers even more, which isn't necessarily an improvement.

tips.en: Part of the reason … Another factor structures two causes.
tips.kk: Part of the reason … Another factor — екі себепті құрылым.
tips.ru: Part of the reason … Another factor — структура с двумя причинами.
tips.example: Another factor is that many people feel traditional media represent official views

tips.en: Ironically … not necessarily an improvement is a mature conclusion.
tips.kk: Ironically … not necessarily an improvement — парасатты қорытынды.
tips.ru: Ironically … not necessarily an improvement — зрелый вывод.

questions.question: Do you think people trust traditional media less than before?

text: For some things, yes. I think there should be clear limits on content that encourages violence or targets children with harmful advertising, for example. But I'd be wary of rules that are too broad, because they could easily be used to silence criticism or opinions that the authorities don't like. The best rules are specific, transparent and decided openly, not behind closed doors.

tips.en: Concrete examples of what should be limited.
tips.kk: Нені шектеу керек екенінің нақты мысалдары.
tips.ru: Конкретные примеры того, что стоит ограничить.
tips.example: content that encourages violence or targets children with harmful advertising

tips.en: I'd be wary of … The best rules are … gives a concern, then a solution.
tips.kk: I'd be wary of … The best rules are … — алаңдаушылық, сосын шешім.
tips.ru: I'd be wary of … The best rules are … — опасение, затем решение.
tips.example: I'd be wary of rules that are too broad

questions.question: Should there be stricter rules about what can be broadcast?

text: Enormously. Most young people hardly watch scheduled TV at all; they watch what they want, when they want, usually on a phone. Content has also become much shorter — a lot of people get their news from one-minute videos rather than full articles. The positive side is choice and access. The negative side is that short formats can oversimplify complicated issues, and people rarely hear views they disagree with.

tips.en: When they watch and how long content is — two concrete shifts.
tips.kk: Қашан көреді және мазмұн қандай ұзындықта — екі нақты өзгеріс.
tips.ru: Когда смотрят и какой длины контент — два конкретных сдвига.
tips.example: Content has also become much shorter

tips.en: The positive side … The negative side gives a balanced ending.
tips.kk: The positive side … The negative side — симметриялы қорытынды.
tips.ru: The positive side … The negative side — симметричный итог.
tips.example: The negative side is that short formats can oversimplify complicated issues

phrases.text: what they want, when they want

note.en: “Make something seem simpler than it is”.
